questions.question: What main truth is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: It explains absolute lordship and shows that Allah alone controls, cares for, and manages the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be seen all through the universe, especially in living things?
questions.answer: It says a wise and merciful hidden action can be seen everywhere, especially in how living things are raised and looked after.

questions.question: What does the passage say this universal care proves?
questions.answer: It proves the reality of a complete and unlimited lordship.

questions.question: Why can this kind of lordship not have any partner?
questions.answer: Because sharing it would ruin its purposes and go against its very nature.

questions.question: What are some goals of this lordship mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They include showing beauty, making perfection known, displaying valuable works, and revealing hidden skills.

questions.question: Where are those goals especially gathered and shown?
questions.answer: They are focused in individual things and in living beings.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would happen if even the smallest thing were linked to a partner besides Allah?
questions.answer: The purposes of lordship would be blocked and those goals would be damaged.

questions.question: How would turning people toward causes instead of Allah oppose this truth?
questions.answer: It would pull aware beings away from Allah and from the purposes He intended.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the Qur’an’s many statements praising Allah’s purity and greatness?
questions.answer: They guide people again and again to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the overall lesson about Allah’s unity in this passage?
questions.answer: Since one Lord manages everything wisely and mercifully, no partner can share His rule.

questions.question: Which title is given to the second truth in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called absolute dominicality, meaning Allah’s complete lordship.

questions.question: What kind of “hand” is described as working everywhere in the universe?
questions.answer: A hidden hand that acts with wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: In what two ways does the passage describe this working in creation?
questions.answer: It says it is found everywhere in the same general way, yet it also appears in surprising forms.

questions.question: How does the passage use living things to support its message?
questions.answer: It points to how they are nurtured and developed as evidence of Allah’s care and control.

questions.question: Why would assigning a partner to Allah harm the meaning of lordship?
questions.answer: Because it would interfere with the showing of Allah’s beauty, perfection, and skill in creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage pay attention to small and particular things?
questions.answer: Because even the smallest living thing displays these divine purposes clearly.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does absolute lordship view that mistake?
questions.answer: It rejects it completely because it clashes with the truth of Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What role does the Qur’an play at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as a steady guide that directs people to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does it mean that this guidance is found even in the Qur’an’s letters and their forms?
questions.answer: It means the message of tawhid is deeply woven throughout the Qur’an.

questions.question: What central belief should a student take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone is the true Lord, and all care, rule, and direction in creation belong only to Him.

questions.question: What evidence from the universe is used first in this passage?
questions.answer: The first evidence is the wise and merciful care seen everywhere in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say this care is an outflow or reflection of?
questions.answer: It is a reflection of Allah’s complete lordship.

questions.question: What does “absolute” add to the idea of lordship here?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s rule is total, unlimited, and not shared.

questions.question: Name one purpose of lordship mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: One purpose is making divine beauty visible in creation.

questions.question: Name another purpose of lordship mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: Another is making divine perfection known.

questions.question: What else does the passage say lordship brings out in created things?
questions.answer: It brings out precious artistry and hidden excellence.

questions.question: Why would a partner ruin these purposes?
questions.answer: Because sharing the act with another would blur the true source of those qualities and spoil their meaning.

questions.question: How would this affect conscious beings?
questions.answer: They would be directed away from Allah and toward created causes.

questions.question: What final support is brought from the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The passage says the Qur’an constantly points people to Allah’s transcendence and unity.

questions.question: How do the beginning and ending of the passage connect?
questions.answer: It begins with signs of care in the universe and ends by showing that the Qur’an confirms that those signs lead to tawhid.

questions.question: What quality of Allah’s rule is emphasized by the word “dominicality” in this passage?
questions.answer: It emphasizes Allah’s nurturing, governing, and raising of creation.

questions.question: Where does the passage say this rule can be noticed most clearly?
questions.answer: It can be noticed throughout the universe, especially in living beings.

questions.question: What two qualities describe the way this rule appears?
questions.answer: It appears with wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: What does the regular care of creation show about the One behind it?
questions.answer: It shows that the One behind it has real and complete lordship.

questions.question: Why is partnership impossible in that lordship according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because the goals of that lordship require full control and cannot be split.

questions.question: What are those goals concerned with showing?
questions.answer: They are concerned with showing beauty, excellence, artistry, and hidden wonders.

questions.question: Why are individual creatures important in this discussion?
questions.answer: Because those goals are concentrated in single creatures and living beings.

questions.question: How does the passage describe such a turn?
questions.answer: It describes it as opposite and hostile to the essence of lordship.

questions.question: What does the passage say absolute lordship would never allow?
questions.answer: It would never allow acceptance of partners.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an described in relation to Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It is described as a constant guide leading people to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the main cause-and-effect message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Since all creation is cared for by one wise and merciful Lord, it follows that no one shares His lordship.

questions.question: What is the “second truth” trying to prove?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove Allah’s oneness through His complete lordship over creation.

questions.question: What pattern in the universe supports this truth?
questions.answer: A pattern of wise and merciful care appears everywhere.

questions.question: What example does the passage give special attention to within creation?
questions.answer: It especially points to living things and how they grow and are cared for.

questions.question: Why is the same kind of care appearing everywhere important?
questions.answer: It shows a single source of control rather than many separate rulers.

questions.question: What does the passage say are gathered together in small, living things?
questions.answer: The important aims of lordship are gathered together in them.

questions.question: What are some of those aims?
questions.answer: They include displaying beauty, showing perfection, and making fine artistry known.

questions.question: What would be the result of connecting even one tiny creature to a partner besides Allah?
questions.answer: It would damage those aims and keep them from being fulfilled.

questions.question: How would this affect people who are aware and able to think?
questions.answer: It would direct their attention away from Allah and toward secondary causes.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s language and structure?
questions.answer: It says even its smallest parts point people toward Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What short summary best fits this passage?
questions.answer: The order and care seen in all things show one Lord, so Allah has no partner.

questions.question: In simple words, what does “absolute dominicality” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means Allah fully owns, runs, and cares for creation by Himself.

questions.question: What sign of this truth is seen across the whole cosmos?
questions.answer: The sign is the universal care and development of created things.

questions.question: Which group of created beings is mentioned especially as an example?
questions.answer: Living beings are mentioned especially.

questions.question: What makes this care more than ordinary or random?
questions.answer: It is full of wisdom, mercy, and order.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from that kind of care?
questions.answer: It concludes that there is one true Lord whose rule is complete.

questions.question: Why does complete lordship rule out partners?
questions.answer: Because its goals can only be achieved if all authority belongs to one Lord.

questions.question: What goals are listed to explain this point?
questions.answer: The passage lists showing beauty, announcing perfection, displaying art, and uncovering hidden excellence.

questions.question: Why would even a tiny shared role be a problem?
questions.answer: Because even that would spoil the message and purpose found in creation.

questions.question: What wrong direction could conscious beings be pushed toward?
questions.answer: They could be pushed to look at causes instead of Allah.

questions.question: Why is that direction against the truth of lordship?
questions.answer: Because lordship is meant to lead people to the One who truly plans, gives, and governs.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an help protect people from that mistake?
questions.answer: It repeatedly points them to Allah’s purity, greatness, and oneness.

questions.question: After reading this passage, what belief should become stronger?
questions.answer: A person’s belief that Allah alone is the Lord and that no partner shares His rule should become stronger.
